title: Sheaves of rings are ring objects of abelian sheaves
statement:
In the situation of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-presheaf], let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on
$C$. Then its underlying abelian presheaf $\mathcal R_{\Ab}$ is a sheaf, and it carries a unique
ring object structure in $\Sh(C,\Ab)$ such that the counit isomorphism
$a(\mathcal R_{\Ab})\cong\mathcal R_{\Ab}$ is an isomorphism of ring objects, where
$a(\mathcal R_{\Ab})$ has the structure of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-presheaf]. Concretely, its
multiplication $\mathcal R_{\Ab}\otimes\mathcal R_{\Ab}=a(\mathcal R_{\Ab}\otimes_p\mathcal R_{\Ab})\to\mathcal R_{\Ab}$
is the unique morphism of sheaves extending the objectwise ring multiplication, and its unit
$\underline{\mathbf Z}\to\mathcal R_{\Ab}$ is the unique morphism extending $n\mapsto n\cdot1$. It is
commutative when all rings $\mathcal R(U)$ are commutative, and a morphism of sheaves of rings is
a morphism of ring objects.

proof.text: Put $S=\mathcal R_{\Ab}$ and write $i$ for the inclusion of abelian sheaves in abelian presheaves. Forgetting the ring operations does not change the section sets or the restriction functions. Consequently a compatible family of sections of $S$ on a covering sieve is exactly a compatible family for $\mathcal R$, and has the same unique glued section. Gluing is additive: the sum of the glued sections of two families restricts to the sum of those families, hence is their sum's glued section by uniqueness; zero and negatives behave in the same way. Thus the matching-family bijection is an isomorphism of abelian groups, and $S$ is an abelian sheaf. This is the direct matching-family argument underlying Stacks Tag 00YR, not an appeal to an uncited preservation-of-limits theorem.

source.place: Tag 00YR, section-sheaves-algebraic-structures, assertion (alpha) and the description of rings as sextuples

proof.text: Use the sheafification universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], with values in abelian groups. Write $t_F:F\to iaF$ for its universal map. The identity of $iS$ extends uniquely to $e:a(iS)\to S$, so $i(e)t_{iS}=1_{iS}$. Since the inclusion is full, $t_{iS}$ itself is a sheaf morphism $q:S\to a(iS)$. Then $eq=1_S$, while $qe=1_{a(iS)}$: both latter maps have the same composite with $t_{iS}$, and uniqueness of extension proves equality. Hence $e$ is the counit isomorphism and $i(q)=t_{iS}$. Naturality, to be used below, follows from the same uniqueness: for $h:F\to G$, $i(ah)t_F=t_Gh$, since both sides are the extension data defining $ah$.

source.place: First paragraph, counit isomorphism; Stacks Tags 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint) and 00YR, assertion (epsilon)

proof.text: Let $P=iS$ be the abelian presheaf underlying $\mathcal R$. Apply [det-def-sfb-ring-object-presheaf] to this presheaf of rings. It gives the ring object $A=aP$, with multiplication $m=a(\mu_p)\circ c_{P,P}$ and unit $u=a(\eta_p)$, where $\mu_p:P\otimes_pP\to P$ and $\eta_p:\underline{\mathbf Z}_p\to P$ are the objectwise ring maps, $c_{P,P}:aP\otimes aP\xrightarrow{\sim}a(P\otimes_pP)$ is the strong monoidal comparison, and the unit of the sheaf category is $a(\underline{\mathbf Z}_p)$. It also gives commutativity of $A$ when the section rings are commutative, and preservation of ring-object structures by the sheafification of any presheaf ring morphism.

source.place: First paragraph, ring-object structure on the sheafification from det-def-sfb-ring-object-presheaf

proof.text: Define $\mu=e\circ m\circ(q\otimes q)$ and $\eta=e\circ u$, using $e:A\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ and $q=e^{-1}$ from step 2. Check the equations of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid] explicitly. If $Q=((q\otimes q)\otimes q)$, cancellation of $qe$ and tensor functoriality give $\mu(\mu\otimes1_S)=e\,m(m\otimes1_A)Q$; naturality of the associator gives $\mu(1_S\otimes\mu)\alpha_S=e\,m(1_A\otimes m)\alpha_AQ$. These agree by associativity of $m$. The left unit composite is $\mu(\eta\otimes1_S)=e\,m(u\otimes1_A)(1_{\mathbf1}\otimes q)=e\lambda_A(1_{\mathbf1}\otimes q)=\lambda_S$, by naturality of the unitor; the right unit composite is $e\,m(1_A\otimes u)(q\otimes1_{\mathbf1})=e\rho_A(q\otimes1_{\mathbf1})=\rho_S$. Also $\mu(e\otimes e)=em$ and $\eta=eu$, so $e$ is a ring-object morphism; the inverse identities $q\mu=m(q\otimes q)$ and $q\eta=u$ make $q$ one as well. Any other structure making $e$ a morphism must satisfy these same two equations, and cancellation of $e\otimes e$ forces precisely $\mu=e m(q\otimes q)$ and $\eta=eu$. This proves the required uniqueness.

source.place: First paragraph, explicit conjugation, its axioms and uniqueness

proof.text: Identify these structure maps with the asserted extensions. By [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], $S\otimes S=a(P\otimes_pP)$, the tensor of sheaf morphisms is the sheafification of their presheaf tensor. Clause 3 of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso] ensures that the unit-induced tensor comparison is invertible after sheafification; the canonical strong monoidal comparison $c_{P,P}$ of the specified tensor construction is its inverse, namely the inverse of $a(t_P\otimes_p t_P):a(P\otimes_pP)\to a(iaP\otimes_piaP)=A\otimes A$. The identification $i(q)=t_P$ from step 2 therefore gives $c_{P,P}(q\otimes q)=1_{a(P\otimes_pP)}$. Substituting into step 4 yields $\mu=e\,a(\mu_p)$, while $\eta=e\,a(\eta_p)$ already. Naturality of $t$ now gives $i(\mu)t_{P\otimes_pP}=i(e)i(a\mu_p)t_{P\otimes_pP}=i(e)t_P\mu_p=\mu_p$, and likewise $i(\eta)t_{\underline{\mathbf Z}_p}=\eta_p$. Since $S$ is a sheaf, [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] says that extension through either universal map is unique. Thus the product extends $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$ and the unit extends $n\mapsto n\cdot1$, with the integer presheaf distinguished from its sheafification.

source.place: First paragraph, concrete multiplication and unit; canonical comparison of det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure

proof.text: If every section ring is commutative, step 3 gives $m\beta_{A,A}=m$. Naturality of the sheaf symmetry and the formula of step 4 imply $\mu\beta_{S,S}=e\,m(q\otimes q)\beta_{S,S}=e\,m\beta_{A,A}(q\otimes q)=\mu$. This is exactly the commutativity condition of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid]. No commutativity assumption was used in the construction or the associativity and unit checks.

Let $f:\mathcal R\to\mathcal R'$ be a sheaf ring morphism, and denote its underlying presheaf map by $f_p:P\to P'$. It is a presheaf ring morphism, so [det-def-sfb-ring-object-presheaf] gives $f_p\mu_p=\mu'_p(f_p\otimes_p f_p)$ and $f_p\eta_p=\eta'_p$. The maps $f\mu$ and $\mu'(f\otimes f)$ from $a(P\otimes_pP)$ to the target sheaf have equal composites with $t_{P\otimes_pP}$: for the first this is $f_p\mu_p$ by step 5; for the second it is $\mu'_p(f_p\otimes_p f_p)$, by naturality of $t$ and the formula $f\otimes f=a(f_p\otimes_p f_p)$ of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure]. Uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] gives $f\mu=\mu'(f\otimes f)$. Similarly the two maps $f\eta,\eta'$ from $a(\underline{\mathbf Z}_p)$ have the same restriction $f_p\eta_p=\eta'_p$, hence agree. These are the two morphism equations of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid], proving the last clause.

source.place: Second paragraph, preservation of multiplication and unit by sheaf ring morphisms, using the equivalent unique-extension argument

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs; explicit matching families, universal-property argument, conjugation identities and strong-monoidal comparison calculation
